params.body:
The read token lives on a laptop, and a laptop travels and opens links. Until now whoever held it could read `brief/{slug}` for every project: the access codes of seventeen client systems, the internal notes, the rates and the unbilled hours, in one call and without a signature. That was the largest thing a stolen laptop was worth, and it is the one piece of tonight's work that also protects the Mac as it is today.

The brief now answers in two sizes.

- Status stays open on the read token: title, next action, stack, milestones, links, subscriptions, attachments, updates, evolution. A session that cannot read status is a session that guesses.
- Access codes, internal notes, finance, unbilled hours, time entries and expenses need the operator's word: the same admission a proposal needs, signed on the YubiKey or on the project page.
- What is held back is named (`withheld`, `withheldReason`) rather than silently absent. A brief that quietly shrinks reads as a project without codes, and that is the failure this file has warned about since the day silence became an assertion.
- The owner token is unchanged, because it lives in Portal's own `.env`: that is Portal speaking to itself.

Suite 549/550 (the one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which wants a stamp a real deploy writes).
params.title: De brief: status open, de codes achter het woord van de operator
